text: Toward the end of the fifth or sixth month, while the plague raged most fiercely outside, the prince gave a masked ball for his thousand friends. <break time="0.8s" /> It was a splendid party, but first let me tell you about the seven rooms in which it was held. <break time="0.8s" /> In most palaces such rooms form a long, straight line, but here a guest could see little more than one room at a time. <break time="0.8s" /> There was a sharp turn every twenty or thirty yards, and at each turn a new and strange view appeared. <break time="0.8s" /> Each room had tall windows of colored glass, and the color of the glass matched the decorations of the room. <break time="0.8s" /> The first room, at the eastern end, was blue, and the others were purple, green, orange, white, and violet. <break time="0.8s" /> There were no lamps in the rooms, but a brazier, a large metal bowl of fire, burned in the hallway behind each window. <break time="0.8s" /> The seventh room, at the far western end, was covered in black velvet, but its windows were a deep red, the color of blood. <break time="0.8s" /> The firelight shining through the red glass looked so ghostly that few guests were brave enough to step inside. <break time="0.8s" /> It was in this black room that a gigantic clock of ebony stood against the western wall.
